name: Jira
description: Wakes an agent when a Jira Cloud issue changes status, and lets it read what happened. A Team Admin binds their team's Jira site and API token and configures which projects to watch and which status transitions matter (e.g. "In Progress → Ready for Dev"); the broker sidecar holds that credential and polls Jira server-side, so the token never reaches your browser or an agent container. On a matching transition the broker wakes the granted agents and queues the event; the agent drains the queue with the `aee-jira inbox` command-line tool. This replaces the reverted built-in Jira integration (PR #1539) with an installable, uninstallable plugin — removing it leaves the platform byte-identical. Jira Server / Data Center is not supported; there is no two-way sync.

credentials.description: Jira Cloud site — a bare subdomain ("acme") or a full origin ("https://acme.atlassian.net")
Atlassian account e-mail — the Basic-Auth username for the API token
Jira API token — held only by the broker sidecar, never returned after it is set

promptLine: When a watched Jira issue changes status you are woken; run `aee-jira inbox` to see the queued status-change events (`aee-jira inbox --consume` drains them — use it once per wake), or `aee-jira whoami` for your plugin scope. All Jira access is server-side in the broker; you never see the Jira token.
